title: In the garden
description: Name the things in a garden, and say what you do there.
grammar: gender and articles, and regular -ar verbs
grammarNote: Most of the verbs in a garden are -ar verbs, and they work the way you already know.

explanation.summary: A garden is a place with living things in it, so it has its own nouns. And almost everything you do in a garden is an -ar verb: regar, plantar, cortar, mirar.

sections.heading: The nouns
sections.body: El árbol, el arbusto, el riego and el huerto are masculine. La flor, la hierba, la tierra, la semilla, el guante and la tijera are not all the same: el guante is masculine and la tijera is feminine, even though both end in -e. The ending is a guide, not a rule.

sections.heading: What you do there
sections.body: An -ar verb drops the -ar and takes the ending that matches the person: yo riego, tú riegas, él riega. The plural of these nouns works as you saw: el árbol becomes los árboles and la flor becomes las flores.

examples.es: hay una semilla en la tierra
examples.en: there is a seed in the earth

items.note: Masculine: el árbol. The plural is los árboles.
Masculine: el riego. It is also the word for I water.
Feminine: la tijera. It is usually plural: las tijeras.

drills.note: Flor is feminine, so las flores.

drills.meaning: I need a pair of scissors to cut
drills.note: Tijera is feminine, so una tijera.
